reasoning: OBSERVATION HOLDS. curl -A Chrome -H 'Accept-Encoding: identity' https://ryan-realty.com/cities/bend -> 200, size_download=3,773,879 (reader: 3,773,835). Decomposed the saved ours-cities_bend.html: 105 self.__next_f.push chunks = 2,057,485 B; the largest (1,305,893 B) is the V3Atlas client props: dots 660,788 B (1,664 dots: 708 active / 628 sold / 328 pending, each with photo URL, href, lat/lng, price, street, beds/baths/sqft), regions+childRegions 276,736 B (9,613 lon/lat pairs at avg 7.7 decimals), amenities 327,127 B (parks/trails MultiPolygons, 10,908 pairs at avg 8.5 decimals). Second chunk (451,053 B) is the PlaceSubdivisionMap props: rail + 711 homes with photos. Body without scripts is 1,687,167 B, of which the server-drawn atlas SVG (class v3-atlas__svg) is 898,760 B (305,017 B of path d=) and the #homes rail ~609 KB with 741 anchors / 787 . So the listing population is serialized three times (atlas dots RSC, homes RSC, homes HTML) and polygons are ~604 KB of RSC plus the SVG paths; the 'polygon' part is real but the larger driver is the uncapped listing population, not geometry. SEVERITY ATTACK. (1) The 3.8 MB vs 1.5 MB comparison is uncompressed. On the wire with 'Accept-Encoding: br, gzip': /cities/bend = 575,755 B (content-encoding: br, x-vercel-cache: HIT, x-nextjs-prerender: 1, cache-control s-maxage=60 swr=600, time_total 0.32 s); redfin.com/city/1387/OR/Bend = 289,807 B (gzip); /cities/bend/awbrey-butte = 417,306 B (br); enjoybendlife.com/bend/awbrey-butte = 40,192 B (gzip); /communities/tetherow = 145,895 B (br); Redfin's Tetherow URL now 404s so no pair. Ratio on the wire: ~2x Redfin for the city, ~10x enjoybendlife for the neighborhood; the absolute number a crawler transfers is 6.5x smaller than the finding states and every place page is prerendered and CDN-cached, so there is no origin render per crawl. (2) Crawl-budget causation is speculative. Google's crawl-budget doc (fetched: https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawl-budget) scopes the guide to 'Large sites (1 million+ unique pages)', 'Medium or larger sites (10,000+ unique pages) with very rapidly changing content (daily)', or sites with a large 'Discovered - currently not indexed' share; the only speed line is soft: 'If Google can load and render your pages faster, we might be able to read more content from your site.' Live sitemaps count 9,292 URLs (core 205 + geo 4,827 [2,642 subdivisions, 18 parks, 55 schools] + listings 3,283 + matrix 885 + content 92). No crawl-stats or index-coverage evidence exists anywhere in the audit scratchpad (tracking/notes.md:77: no URL Inspection or Index Coverage pull in code). (3) Converting: in the saved HTML the is 13,789 B, the hero sits at byte 56,393, the first __next_f chunk at byte 1,709,424, #homes at 979,353 - the LCP image is discovered in the first ~57 KB, so HTML weight delays hydration/INP and phone bandwidth, not LCP discovery. RUM city-class p75 LCP 4,400 ms (tracking/notes.md:73, n=839, TTFB p75 658) cannot be attributed to HTML bytes from this evidence. lighthouserc.cjs:76-83,184-190 records /cities/bend and /cities/bend/awbrey-butte as Tier 1 'Heaviest: embedded Google Maps + recharts' at warn-only perf>=0.65 / LCP<=4200 - a documented acceptance that these are the heavy pages. FIX VS CANON. (a) 'Cap listing cards (24-48)': fold cards are already capped - lib/place/first-look.ts:22 CITY_LOOK_PIN_CAP = 36, capLookListings at :174, used app/cities/[slug]/page.tsx:980. The uncapped things are the atlas dots and the PlaceSubdivisionHomes carousel (components/site/v3/PlaceSubdivisionMap.client.tsx:220-260 renders every home in `homes`; page.tsx:812 placeHomes = all stock rows). Capping the MAP population contradicts the recorded Matt ruling at page.tsx:363-367 ('Matt 2026-09-01: heat maps on every page. Population = every active, pending, and 30-day-closed listing inside the recorded city boundary') and PLACE_PAGES.md:95 'We win with Atlas + live pins'; capping the CAROUSEL with a door to /homes-for-sale/bend does not (PLACE_PAGES.md:56 asks for 'One Field of this place's houses', SITE_PAGES.md:90 'Same Field as /homes-for-sale?city=bend', kill list :76 'Duplicate counts in three places'). (b) 'polygon geometry as static JSON/PMTiles fetched by the map client' cuts against canon: the atlas is server-drawn SVG (V3Atlas.client.tsx:549-651 ringsToPath/outerRings; SITE-82 comment page.tsx:1019-1020 'Atlas owns the drawing'), docs/MASTER_SPEC.md:895 records boundary_geojson 'should be server-rendered, not client-fetched', and the reader itself credits ours as fully server-rendered. The DAL (lib/data/geo/getBoundaryGeoJSON.ts:75-78) returns raw ST_AsGeoJSON with no simplification or quantization, which is the actual defect: 8-9 decimal coordinates are sub-millimetre precision drawn into a 1000-px viewBox. (c) '< 600 KB HTML on every place page' is unreachable while the atlas SVG alone is 899 KB uncompressed on Bend; it would force removing the server-drawn map. (d) 'add a size gate to the route shots': the gate already exists - scripts/check-page-payload-budget.mjs (`ci:page-payload`, shrink-only ratchet on identity bytes, runs in .github/workflows/ci.yml:117 after route smoke against a built server) - but its PAGES list (:64-66) holds only /homes-for-sale (baseline 1,019,774). The work graph already states 'page payload must hold or improve' as a product hold on every class node (scripts/seed-site-queue.ts:696-806) and 'ci:page-payload does not regress on any route' (:608), which the gate cannot enforce for routes it does not list - that is the one loop-integrity gap this finding actually exposes. G31 (check-boundary-map.mjs) fires only on , so it does not constrain this route. VERDICT: the weight is real and 2-10x the portals on the wire, but the stated harm (crawl budget, fewer pages sampled) is unsupported for a 9.3K-URL prerendered CDN-cached site and the fix as proposed contradicts two recorded rulings and duplicates an existing gate. Downgrade to minor with the fix corrected.

The weight is the listing population serialized three times (1,664 atlas dots with photo+card fields in RSC, 711 homes as RSC props, 741 home cards in HTML) plus ~604 KB of raw 8-9-decimal polygon coordinates passed to the client atlas on top of the 899 KB server-drawn SVG. This costs phone bandwidth and hydration time, not crawl budget: the site has 9,292 sitemap URLs, well under Google's stated crawl-budget scope, and no crawl-stats evidence exists. corrected_fix: (1) Add /cities/bend, /cities/bend/awbrey-butte, /cities/redmond, /communities/tetherow and /team to PAGES in scripts/check-page-payload-budget.mjs and run --write-baseline against a built server; the shrink-only ratchet already runs in ci.yml after route smoke, so no new gate. (2) Cut the geometry bytes server-side, keeping the atlas server-drawn: quantize coordinates to 5 decimals and simplify rings to the atlas's 1000-px viewBox tolerance (ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology in the boundary_geojson RPC, or in the DAL before unstable_cache) for regions, childRegions and amenity polygons; pass the client V3Atlas only the simplified rings or pre-projected paths it needs. Do not move polygons to a client-fetched static asset (MASTER_SPEC.md:895; SITE-82 'Atlas owns the drawing'). (3) Slim the atlas dot record to what a pin needs (key, lat, lng, price, type, status, age) and keep the full population - the Matt 2026-09-01 ruling fixes the map population at every active, pending and 30-day-closed listing, so cap fields, not dots. (4) Cap the PlaceSubdivisionHomes carousel (e.g. 36, the existing CITY_LOOK_PIN_CAP, spread-sampled per neighborhood) with a real anchor into /homes-for-sale/<city> for the rest, and stop passing the full homes array as client props when the carousel is capped.
